strain: tetO1B/βActin-tTS transgenic (5-HT1BR conditional KO and littermate controls)

age.evidence: Mice were between ages 3-9 months old at time of testing.

sex.evidence: N = 27 (11 males, 16 females) were used in the c-Fos study. N = 52 mice (31 females, 21 males) were used to assess the acute behavioral effects of psilocybin. N = 155 (60 males, 95 females)... N = 164 mice (61 females, 103 males)...

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin (Cat # 14041, Cayman Chemical), or saline vehicle, was injected intraperitoneally (i.p.) at the dose of 5 mg/kg diluted in saline solution (0.9% NaCl) at a volume of 10 ml/kg.

handling.evidence: No handling protocol described in methods.

group_housing.evidence: weaned at postnatal day (PN) 21 into cages of 2-4 same-sex littermates.

day_night_flipped.evidence: All mice were maintained on a 12:12 light-dark cycle [direction not specified]

assays.assay_description: Mice placed in an open field immediately after i.p. injection; video recorded for 1 h with first 15 min scored manually by three blinded experimenters for head twitch counts.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin... was injected intraperitoneally (i.p.) at the dose of 5 mg/kg

setup_habituation.evidence: Immediately following injections, mice were placed in an open field

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in an open field, and video recording was initiated

food_restriction.evidence: Open field arena; no food in apparatus during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: Open field arena; no water in apparatus during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately following injections, mice were placed in an open field, and video recording was initiated

sample_size.evidence: N = 52 mice (31 females, 21 males) were used to assess the acute behavioral effects of psilocybin.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (5 mg/kg) markedly increased head twitches relative to saline, with no difference between 5-HT1BR KO and control mice and no sex effect, indicating the HTR is independent of 5-HT1BR.
outcomes.statistics: main effect of psilocybin: F(1,28)=312.3; main effect of genotype: F(1,28)=0.4982; sex F(1,24)=0.525, p=0.476
outcomes.evidence: Mice treated with psilocybin demonstrated significantly more head twitch responses than mice treated with saline (Fig. 2A; main effect of psilocybin: F (1,28) = 312.3). However, there was no significant difference in the number of head twitches between genotypes (main effect of genotype: F(1, 28) = 0.4982).

B1_num_measures.evidence: noting the total number of and time stamp of each head twitch

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total head twitch counts reported; no within-session time-course.

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response is excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Animal tested alone in open field.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Three experimenters scored the first 15 min of activity for head twitches

E3_bedding.evidence: Not reported; standard open field has bare floor.

E7_social_context.evidence: Individual testing in the open field.

D1_continuity.evidence: video recording was initiated... for 1 h

D2_session_duration.evidence: video recording was initiated... for 1 h. Three experimenters scored the first 15 min

D5_followup.evidence: Acute test only, starting at injection.

assays.assay_description: Mice placed in open field immediately post-injection; locomotion scored over 30-60 min via EthoVision; AUC of distance computed.

setup_habituation.evidence: Immediately following injections, mice were placed in an open field

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed in an open field and moved freely.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in open field apparatus during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in open field apparatus during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately following injections, mice were placed in an open field

sample_size.evidence: N = 52 mice (31 females, 21 males) were used to assess the acute behavioral effects of psilocybin.

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin reduced locomotion over the first 30 min in control mice (significant by AUC), with attenuated effect in 5-HT1BR KO (no significant reduction); genotype x drug interaction did not reach significance. No effect on velocity.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin significantly decreased locomotion in the 30 min following administration (F(1,48) = 8.18, p < 0.0063)... significant reductions in locomotor activity following psilocybin in control (t28 = 2.92, p = 0.0068), but not in 5-HT1BR KO mice (t20 = 1.26, p = 0.16).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Locomotion was scored with EthoVision software [distance and velocity reported]

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Locomotor activity is shown for... mice over the 30 min following administration (Fig. 2B, binned over time)

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotor distance is not an ethological behaviour per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: EthoVision is a position-tracker (score 0 per rubric).

E3_bedding.evidence: Standard open field; no bedding mentioned.

E6_spatial.evidence: Open field is a single arena.

D1_continuity.evidence: video recording was initiated... for 1 h

D2_session_duration.evidence: video recording was initiated... for 1 h

assays.assay_description: Davis Rig 16-bottle gustometer; mice tested individually for 30 min with 6 bottles (water + 2,4,6,8,10% sucrose), each presented up to 120 s; total licks per concentration recorded via capacitance system; performed 24 h after psilocybin in both chronic corticosterone and behavioral despair cohorts.

application_type.evidence: Mice were injected with psilocybin (5 mg/kg, i.p) or saline vehicle

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were water-restricted for 5 days of initial training... On day 1... day 2... day 3... final training day

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed individually in the gustometer

food_restriction.evidence: Mice were then food restricted for 2 days before being individually returned to the gustometer

water_restriction.evidence: Mice were water-restricted for 5 days of initial training

time_to_assay.evidence: The 6 bottle paradigm was then repeated 24 h after drug administration for the experimental gustometer test.

sample_size.evidence: N = 155 (60 males, 95 females) and N = 164 (61 females, 103 males) cohorts contributed to gustometer testing across paradigms.

outcomes.summary: In female mice psilocybin increased licking for sucrose (particularly 10%) in control but not in 5-HT1BR KO mice; in male mice no effect under chronic corticosterone, but in the behavioral despair model psilocybin increased 10% sucrose licking in controls of both sexes and had no effect in KO mice.
outcomes.evidence: In female mice, psilocybin significantly increased hedonic responding in the gustometer as measured by increased licking for sucrose... there was no effect in female mice lacking 5-HT1BR... In male mice... no effects of psilocybin on... chronic corticosterone-induced behavioral effects... In control mice [despair], there was a significant effect of treatment on sucrose consumption.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total licks at each tube were recorded; analyses across 6 concentrations and separately at 10%.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total licks per concentration; no within-session time bins reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Lick count is a consummatory measure but assay does not score distinct ethological acts.

B5_social.evidence: Mice tested individually; no social construct.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Sucrose preference is innate hedonic responding.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Capacitance-based lick detection (Med Associates Davis Rig — score 0 per rubric).

E1_environment_type.evidence: A Davis Rig 16-bottle Gustometer (Med Associates MED-DAV160 M) was used

E6_spatial.evidence: Single chamber with rotating bottle access.

E8_food_water.evidence: access to water, 2% sucrose, 4% sucrose, 6% sucrose, 8% sucrose, and 10% sucrose

D1_continuity.evidence: returned to the gustometer for 30 min... repeated 24 h after drug administration

D3_recording_days.evidence: Experimental gustometer test conducted once (24 h post-drug); training days excluded.

D4_baseline.evidence: Training sessions not analyzed as pre-drug baseline data for the experimental contrast.

D5_followup.evidence: Test 24 h after psilocybin injection (>=24 h post-dose).

assays.assay_description: Arena (~20x16 in) with ~24 cm corn bedding, food pellet on white platform under bright lamp (~120 lux); latency to bite recorded over 5 min; home-cage latency measured immediately after as hunger control.

application_type.evidence: Mice were injected with psilocybin (5 mg/kg, i.p) or saline vehicle

setup_habituation.evidence: Thirty minutes before testing, mice were placed individually into holding cages [room/cage acclimation, not apparatus habituation]

setup_restrain.evidence: Each mouse was placed in the same corner of the arena, facing the wall

food_restriction.evidence: mice were allowed food that day until 24 h before the time of the novelty-suppressed feeding test

water_restriction.evidence: No water in NSF arena during the 5-min test.

time_to_assay.evidence: The NSF was performed 24 h after the gustometer in the corticosterone stress paradigm [~48 h post-drug], and 48 h after the EPM in the chronic behavioral despair paradigm [~96 h post-drug].

sample_size.evidence: Drawn from N=155 (cort) and N=164 (despair) cohorts.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin decreased latency to eat in control mice (anxiolytic) but not in 5-HT1BR KO mice. In the chronic corticosterone model the effect appeared only in females; in the behavioral despair model the effect occurred in both sexes (sex effects not significant). No effects on homecage latency.
outcomes.statistics: Females cort genotype x drug F(2,72)=2.99, p=0.049; controls χ²=9.62, p=0.002; KO χ²=1.85, p=0.174. Despair χ5=31.40, p<0.0001; controls χ1=6.41, p=0.011; KO χ1=1.70, p=0.19
outcomes.evidence: control mice injected with psilocybin showed reduced latency to eat compared to saline-treated mice (Fig. 3D, χ² = 9.62, p = 0.002), while we saw no significant effect in the 5-HT1BR KO mice (Fig. 3D, χ² = 1.85, p = 0.174).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Latency in arena and latency in home cage were recorded.

B4_ethological.evidence: Feeding (biting the pellet) is a natural consummatory behaviour directly measured.

E1_environment_type.evidence: rodent transport container (20'x16') ... to serve as an arena

E2_shelter.evidence: Open arena with central platform; no enclosed refuge.

E3_bedding.evidence: floor covered with approximately 24 cm of corn bedding

E8_food_water.evidence: a single pellet of food was placed on a white platform... in the center of the arena

D1_continuity.evidence: recorded over a session of 5 min

D5_followup.evidence: NSF performed 48-96 h after psilocybin injection.

assays.assay_description: Standard EPM (4 arms, 35x5 cm, 60 cm above ground; closed arms with 20 cm walls, open arms 1 cm lip); 6 min trial; entries and time in each arm scored via EthoVision. Used across chronic cort, behavioral despair, adult-knockdown and GR127935 antagonist cohorts.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin 5 mg/kg i.p.; in the antagonist experiment, GR127935 (10 mg/kg, i.p.) was given 30 min prior to psilocybin (both i.p.).

setup_habituation.evidence: No apparatus pre-exposure described for EPM.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to explore the maze undisturbed for 6 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in EPM apparatus during 6-min test.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in EPM apparatus during 6-min test.

time_to_assay.evidence: EPM was performed 24 h after the NSF in the corticosterone stress paradigm [~72 h post-drug] and 24 h after the gustometer in the chronic behavioral despair paradigm [~48 h post-drug]; antagonist EPM also performed within this window.

sample_size.evidence: Drawn from N=155 (cort), N=164 (despair), N=43 (antagonist), N=30 (adult KO) cohorts.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin increased open-arm entries (anxiolytic) in control mice across stress paradigms — significant in females under chronic cort and in both sexes under behavioral despair — but not in 5-HT1BR KO mice. Pretreatment with the 5-HT1B/1D antagonist GR127935 blocked the anxiolytic effect, and adult 5-HT1BR knockdown also blocked psilocybin's effect.
outcomes.statistics: Females cort: drug x genotype F(1,51)=4.080, p=0.0487; controls p=0.01; KO p=0.732. Despair: genotype x treatment F(2,155)=4.22, p=0.016; controls stress vs stress/psilo p=0.03; KO p=0.99. Antagonist: pretreatment x psilocybin F(1,48)=4.30, p=0.044; controls p=0.0084; GR127935 p=0.89.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin administration significantly decreased anxiety in female control mice, as measured by increased entries in open arms (p = 0.01), but not in mice lacking 5-HT1BR (p = 0.732)... pre-treatment with GR127935, the effect of psilocybin was blocked (p = 0.89).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Behavior was scored using EthoVision software for the number of entries and time spent in each arm.

B4_ethological.evidence: Zone preference/entry counts are spatial measures, not ethological behaviours per rubric.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Elevated plus maze with four arms.

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms not counted as shelter per rubric.

E6_spatial.evidence: Per rubric: EPM scored 0 for spatial complexity.

D1_continuity.evidence: allowed to explore the maze undisturbed for 6 min

judge_notes: Treated head-twitch scoring and locomotor scoring done from the same 1-h open-field video as two separate assays (different behavioural domains, different scoring methods), consistent with all three candidates.

Merged chronic-corticosterone, behavioral-despair, adult-knockdown, and GR127935 antagonist EPM/NSF/gustometer cohorts into the respective single assays per rubric (same paradigm under different manipulations = 1 assay).

B4 ethological for NSF scored Yes because feeding (biting a food pellet) is a directly measured consummatory behaviour from the natural repertoire; gustometer B4 kept No since only total lick count is reported.
Gustometer D5 set Yes (test 24 h post-dose, >=24 h) — corrected from one candidate.
B7 set 0 throughout (EthoVision and Med Associates are position/beam-break tools per rubric).
Did not create separate assays for the c-Fos brain-wide neural analysis (not a behavioural assay).
